lead.headline: US PROPOSES TARIFFS OF UP TO 25% ON INDIA; 17% RATE TIED TO TRADE DEAL
lead.deck: The USTR has proposed duties of up to 25% on Indian goods, with a possible 17% rate if a reciprocal trade deal is reached. India says it is examining the proposal.
paragraphs: The US Trade Representative has proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods in two Section 301 investigations, with exemptions for certain products. The proposal follows probes into industrial capacity and goods made with forced labour.

The USTR says it may consider a 17% rate if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement addressing the findings. The proposal is not yet a final tariff decision; India’s Commerce Ministry says it is examining the notice and that trade concerns belong in ongoing negotiations.

image.alt: Narendra Modi and Donald Trump, pictured at a previous meeting, as the US proposes new tariffs on Indian goods.
image.caption: The tariff proposal comes as New Delhi and Washington negotiate a trade agreement. File photo: The Indian Express.

sidebarStory.headline: FLIPKART CEO KALYAN KRISHNAMURTHY TO LEAVE AFTER MORE THAN 11 YEARS
sidebarStory.subhead: The Bengaluru-based retailer says its board and product chief Balaji Thiagarajan will lead in the interim.
paragraphs: Flipkart announced that Kalyan Krishnamurthy is concluding his tenure as chief executive after more than 11 years with the company. Walmart International chief Chris Nicholas credited him with helping the business grow and strengthen its governance.
The company says it will name a successor in the coming weeks. Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the board will lead the organisation in the interim.

image.caption: Kalyan Krishnamurthy is leaving Flipkart after more than 11 years. Photo: Kalyan Krishnamurthy/X / India Today.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru transit, civic services and city life news

stories.headline: KARNATAKA DROPS LALBAGH ROUTE FOR TUNNEL ROAD AFTER PUBLIC PUSHBACK
paragraphs: The state government has dropped plans to acquire about six acres inside Lalbagh for the north–south tunnel road and is considering two alternative alignments, Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said.
The proposed 16.75-km twin-tunnel project would connect Hebbal and Silk Board. The government says it remains committed to moving the route away from the botanical garden.

image.alt: Bengaluru residents take part in a campaign calling for Lalbagh to be protected.
image.caption: Residents joined the “Walk in Lalbagh” campaign to oppose the original route. Photo: The Indian Express.

stories.headline: POLICE SEARCH FOR LAWYER ACCUSED OF KILLING SISTER IN PROPERTY DISPUTE
paragraphs: Police say a 39-year-old woman was allegedly beaten with a cricket bat by her elder brother after a property dispute at Junnasandra, within Bellandur police limits.
Investigators say the accused, a 42-year-old lawyer, fled after the attack and a case has been registered. The family’s two children and mother were at home, according to police.

stories.headline: TWO BENGALURU SCREENINGS OF PAKISTANI SERIAL CANCELLED AFTER BACKLASH
paragraphs: Organisers withdrew two planned private screenings of the Pakistani television serial Dar-e-Nijaat, scheduled for November 28 and December 5, after online criticism.
Police said neither organiser had obtained prior permission and warned against holding the events. Both organisers confirmed the screenings had been cancelled.

image.alt: Poster for the Pakistani television serial Dar-e-Nijaat.
image.caption: The two planned Bengaluru screenings of Dar-e-Nijaat were cancelled. Poster: Instagram / Hindustan Times.

groups.ariaLabel: India courts, diplomacy and public policy news

stories.headline: SUPREME COURT SETS ASIDE ORDER SEEKING PROBE INTO RAHUL GANDHI’S ASSETS
paragraphs: The Supreme Court set aside an Allahabad High Court order directing the CBI and Enforcement Directorate to verify allegations that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi held assets disproportionate to his known income.
The three-judge bench sent the petition back to the High Court for fresh consideration, including whether it is maintainable. It did not decide the underlying allegations.

stories.headline: INDIA AND CHINA HOLD MILITARY-LEVEL TALKS IN ARUNACHAL PRADESH
paragraphs: Military commanders from India and China held a second round of talks in Arunachal Pradesh, focusing on rules for engagement and communication to prevent local friction along the Line of Actual Control from escalating.
The discussions included establishing procedures for interactions in the eastern sector. Officials described the exchanges as aimed at maintaining peace and preventing escalation.

stories.headline: SC SEEKS CENTRE, DELHI RESPONSE ON PLEAS OVER DETENTIONS AT CEC PROTEST
paragraphs: The Supreme Court directed the Centre and Delhi government to file comprehensive responses to petitions alleging that political leaders were illegally detained during an October protest against the Chief Election Commissioner.
The bench gave the authorities ten days to respond. The petitions raise allegations about police action during the demonstration; the court has not ruled on their merits.

groups.ariaLabel: India economy, science and environment news

stories.headline: RBI BULLETIN WARNS FOOD-PRICE PRESSURE MAY KEEP NOVEMBER INFLATION HIGH
paragraphs: An RBI bulletin says broad pressure on food prices may keep retail inflation elevated in November after it crossed 6% in October. The report points to a possible rate increase at the central bank’s December policy review.
The bulletin cited price pressures across most consumption divisions, while warning that energy costs and global uncertainty remain risks.

stories.headline: FIRST INDUSTRY-BUILT PSLV ROCKET NOW TARGETED FOR EARLY 2027
paragraphs: ISRO Chairman V Narayanan says the maiden PSLV-N1 launch, built by a HAL–L&T consortium, is expected in the first quarter of 2027, nearly three years after its original target.
The rocket is ready, but launch timing depends on payload coordination and an available window, according to L&T. The ₹860-crore contract covers five rockets.

image.alt: PSLV launch vehicle representing India’s first industry-built PSLV-N1 programme.
image.caption: The PSLV-N1 launch is waiting on payload coordination and a launch window. Photo: NDTV.

stories.headline: CENTRE GETS UNTIL DECEMBER 10 TO FILE AGAIN ON NICOBAR FOREST RIGHTS
paragraphs: The National Green Tribunal gave the Centre until December 10 to submit fresh material in a case concerning forest rights and clearances for the Great Nicobar development project.
The proposed project includes a transshipment port, township, power plant and airport. The case concerns claims that forest-rights procedures were not properly completed.

groups.ariaLabel: Indian hockey, chess and badminton news

stories.headline: INDIA BEAT JAPAN 4–0, FINISH UNBEATEN AND REACH BEST-EVER WORLD RANKING
paragraphs: India defeated Japan 4–0 to finish the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy league stage with five wins from five and top the standings. Deepika scored twice, with Lalremsiami and Neha adding goals.
The result lifted India to No. 4 in the FIH world rankings, its highest-ever position. India will meet Malaysia in the semi-final on November 27.

stories.headline: GUKESH AND SINDAROV DRAW AGAIN AFTER JUST 20 MOVES
paragraphs: Defending champion D Gukesh and challenger Javokhir Sindarov drew their second World Championship game in Geneva, agreeing to a draw after 20 moves in a London System.
The second successive draw leaves the 14-game match tied 1–1. Game three is scheduled for Thursday.

stories.headline: TREESA JOLLY AND GAYATRI GOPICHAND ADVANCE; PRANNOY EXITS
paragraphs: Two-time defending women’s doubles champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand moved into the last 16 at the Syed Modi India International in Lucknow.
The Wednesday results also saw men’s singles third seed H S Prannoy exit the tournament. The Super 300 event runs through November 29.
